title: What do six sums and differences of integers come to?
description: Six sums and take aways of positive and negative numbers are worked as walks on the number line. The sums start at the first number and move by the sign of the second. The take aways are read as the movement from the second number to the first.
teaching_notes: One idea: a sum is a walk from the first number, and a take away a - b is the movement from b to a on the number line. Watch for students who think subtracting always makes a number smaller.

video_script.why: The child works six sums and differences as walks on the number line, and sees that taking away a negative number moves to the right.
video_script.substitution: The six expressions of the book question, solved in three groups as walks on the number line.
video_script.anchor: the number line of the book, with a walker who can walk beyond ten as the line goes on
video_script.payoff_line: Each sum is a walk from the start, and the sign tells the direction.

final_answer.spoken: negative five, zero, ten, negative ten, fourteen and two

maths_rules: a sum: start at the first number, a positive second number moves right, a negative one moves left
a take away x - y is the movement from y to x (target - start)
c. -10 + 20: 10 steps right to 0, then 10 more, reaches 10
d. 10 - 20: movement from 20 to 10 is 10 steps left, -10
e. 7 - (-7): movement from -7 to 7 is 7 + 7 = 14 steps right, +14
f. -8 - (-10): movement from -10 to -8 is 2 steps right, +2
video_script.design: The number line with a walker; the three sums are walked from the first number, then the three take aways are walked from the second number to the first.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the number line.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Six sums and take aways of positive and negative numbers are given.
<bookmark mark='look'/>In the last one, we take away negative ten from negative eight. Does the answer get smaller?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: start at the first number; + positive moves right; + negative moves left; Target number - Starting number = Movement

marks.sum: the walker starts at the first number, with arrows right for a positive and left for a negative
marks.rule: the line Target number - Starting number = Movement is written

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>In a sum, the walker starts at the first number and moves by the second.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>A take away is the movement needed, the target number take away the starting number.

marks.given: the six expressions are written in two columns

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three sums and three take aways.

beats.on_screen: To find: the value of each

marks.find: the words value of each are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the value of each one.

marks.one: the first group is marked: the sums
marks.a: the walker stays on -5 and -5 is written
marks.b: the walker goes 7 left from 7 to 0 and 0 is written
marks.c: the walker goes 10 right to 0 and 10 more, and 10 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, the sums.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Negative five plus zero. The walker does not move, so it stays at negative five.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Seven plus negative seven. The walker goes seven steps left from seven, and reaches zero.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Negative ten plus twenty. It goes ten steps right to zero, then ten more, and reaches ten.

marks.two: the second group is marked: the take aways, from the second number to the first
marks.d: an arrow runs from 20 left to 10 and -10 is written
marks.e: an arrow runs from -7 to 0 and on to 7, and +14 is written
marks.f: an arrow runs from -10 right to -8 and +2 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, the take aways, read from the second number to the first.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Ten take away twenty. From twenty to ten is ten steps backward, so negative ten.
<bookmark mark='e'/>Seven take away negative seven. From negative seven to seven is seven and seven, so fourteen forward.
<bookmark mark='f'/>Negative eight take away negative ten. From negative ten to negative eight is two steps forward, so positive two.

beats.on_screen: Check: starting number + movement = target number;  20 + (-10) = 10;  -7 + 14 = 7;  -10 + 2 = -8

marks.check: the check line starting number plus movement equals target number is written

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, check the take aways by putting the movement back on the starting number.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Twenty plus negative ten lands on ten.
<bookmark mark='e'/>Negative seven plus fourteen lands on seven.
<bookmark mark='f'/>Negative ten plus two lands on negative eight.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a. -5  b. 0  c. 10  d. -10  e. 14  f. 2

marks.sums: the answers of the three sums are boxed
marks.takes: the answers of the three take aways are boxed
marks.pay: the sign on each move glows

narration: <bookmark mark='sums'/>The sums are negative five, zero and ten.
<bookmark mark='takes'/>The take aways are negative ten, fourteen and two.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Each sum is a walk from the start, and the sign tells the direction.
